quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian paprika isn't just a spice—it's a national treasure! Hungary has eight different grades of paprika, ranging from delicate and sweet to fiery hot. The town of Kalocsa is known as the 'Paprika Capital' and celebrates with colorful festivals every autumn.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Olympic Marmots
short_read.teaser: These charming, whistle-calling creatures are found nowhere else on Earth except the Olympic Mountains. Learn about their unique behaviors and how they survive the long mountain winters.

medium_read.title: How Trees Secretly Talk to Each Other
medium_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that trees communicate through an underground network of fungi, sharing nutrients and even warning each other of danger. This 'wood wide web' reveals forests are far more social than we ever imagined.

long_read.title: The Grand Tour: How Travel Shaped the Modern World
long_read.teaser: For centuries, young Europeans embarked on epic journeys across the continent to complete their education through travel. This fascinating tradition shaped art, architecture, and our very concept of tourism.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season Continues
port_angeles.description: Late summer is still a great time to spot harbor seal pups along the Strait of Juan de Fuca. These adorable youngsters are learning to swim and fish alongside their mothers. Ediz Hook and the waterfront are wonderful spots for gentle seal-watching—just remember to keep a respectful distance!

puzzle_1.question: A ruby-throated hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute while hovering.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're absolutely right—1,200 beats per minute! That tiny heart works incredibly hard.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 1,200 beats per minute—that's about 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are remarkable—they beat about 1,200 times per minute while hovering! That's faster than we can even imagine.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: A hummingbird's heart is about the size of a pencil eraser, yet it beats so fast to power those incredible wings that beat 50-80 times per second. When resting at night, their heart rate drops to as low as 50 beats per minute to conserve energy.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Gyönyörű! (Beautiful!) Pillangó is indeed the Hungarian word for butterfly—such a lovely, musical word!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó'—doesn't it sound beautiful? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and napsugár means sunbeam.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language that isn't related to most European languages—it's part of the Finno-Ugric family. Many Hungarian words are wonderfully descriptive, like pillangó, which seems to flutter off the tongue just like the creature it describes.

puzzle_3.question: What is the Olympic Peninsula's temperate rainforest one of?
options: The only rainforests in the Northern Hemisphere
One of the few temperate rainforests in North America
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! You're right—it's one of the few temperate rainforests in North America, and we're lucky to have it right here! The Hoh and Quinault rainforests receive over 12 feet of rain annually.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The Olympic Peninsula is home to one of the few temperate rainforests in North America! Unlike tropical rainforests, these rare ecosystems thrive in cool, wet climates and are draped in moss and ferns.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Olympic National Park contains some of the largest remaining stands of ancient temperate rainforest in the United States. These forests are filled with Sitka spruce, western hemlock, and bigleaf maple trees covered in thick carpets of moss.
